title: Degree one on a genus-zero proper curve gives the projective line
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a proper integral curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that the canonical map $k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is an isomorphism and that $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$, where cohomology is [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. If there is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] of degree $\deg_k M=1$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], then $C$ is isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf P^1_k$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0C6T, lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree, with degree d=1: the resulting closed immersion into the projective line is an isomorphism since its image is one-dimensional.

proof.text: The curve convention makes C nonempty, integral, and of finite type over k. Its local-ring dimension is one. The stalk-dimension/generalization-chain formula and sobriety identify the supremum of these dimensions with topological Krull dimension: replace each point in a strict generalization chain by its closure, and conversely use the unique generic points of a chain of irreducible closed subsets. Thus C has topological dimension one. The field k is Noetherian (its only ideals are 0 and k), so finite type implies C is Noetherian. For every n>=0 put L_n=M^{\otimes n}, with L_0=O_C. These are invertible, hence quasi-coherent of finite type by their rank-one local trivializations, and therefore coherent.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; preliminaries for the cohomological calculation

proof.text: Proper coherent cohomology is finite-dimensional, and the dimension-one vanishing theorem gives H^q(C,L_n)=0 for q>1. Consequently chi(O_C)=1 by the two hypotheses on O_C. The degree definition gives chi(M)=deg_k(M)+chi(O_C)=2. Since chi(M)=h^0(M)-h^1(M), h^0(M)>=2. Choose a nonzero section s in H^0(C,M).

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; first paragraph, Euler characteristic and choice of s

proof.text: The nonzero-section Cartier lemma says that on every nonempty affine trivialization of M, s=a e with a a nonzero element of a domain. Multiplication by s is therefore injective on every L_n. Define Q_n as its cokernel, obtaining 0 -> L_n -> L_{n+1} -> Q_n -> 0 for n>=0. The local presentation is A --a--> A -> A/(a), with the target trivialized by e^{n+1}. It shows directly that Q_n=Q_0 tensor L_n and that all their supports equal the closed zero set D=Z(s). The coherent-cokernel lemma makes Q_0 coherent. The generic point of the integral C is outside D, since a is nonzero. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of D can be extended strictly by C; since dim C=1, dim D<=0.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; exact sequence of s and its finite zero scheme

proof.text: Euler additivity in 0 -> O_C -> M -> Q_0 -> 0 gives chi(Q_0)=2-1=1. The zero-dimensional-support theorem gives H^q(C,Q_0)=0 for q>0 and dim_k H^0(C,Q_0)=1. The same theorem, applied with the invertible L_n, says that Q_n is coherent with the same support, chi(Q_n)=chi(Q_0)=1, H^q(C,Q_n)=0 for q>0, and dim_k H^0(C,Q_n)=1. In particular D is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; zero-dimensional restriction and Euler characteristic

proof.text: A nonzero q in the one-dimensional k-space H^0(C,Q_0) generates Q_0 as an O_C-module, as follows. Apply the finite-support presentation to Q_0 (and N=O_C): Q_0=i_*G for a closed immersion i:Spec A -> C with A finite-dimensional over k, G coherent, and Gamma(G)=H^0(C,Q_0). The A-linear map A -> Gamma(G), 1 |-> q, is onto because its image already contains the k-span of q, the entire space. The affine tilde functor preserves cokernels and its counit on the quasi-coherent G is an isomorphism; thus O_{Spec A} -> G is onto. At points of this closed subscheme O_C -> i_*O_{Spec A} is onto, so q generates i_*G; outside it Q_0=0. This proves the claim using precisely the cited statements, not a global-generation assertion absent from the zero-dimensional Euler theorem.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; global generation on the Artinian zero scheme

proof.text: The long exact sequence of 0 -> O_C -> M -> Q_0 -> 0 and H^1(C,O_C)=0 lift q to a section t of M. At a point of D, write s=a e and t=b e in a local basis. Since q generates Q_0, b mod a generates the local ring O_{C,x}/(a); hence b is a unit (a lies in the maximal ideal). Off D, a is a unit. Thus s,t generate M everywhere, and on D the restriction of t is a basis of M|_D.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; lifting a generator of the restriction to a second section

proof.text: Induct on n using the exact sequences of step 3 and their cohomology long exact sequences. Starting from H^1(C,L_0)=0, the vanishings H^1(C,Q_n)=0 imply H^1(C,L_{n+1})=0. They also give short exact sequences 0 -> H^0(C,L_n) --s--> H^0(C,L_{n+1}) -> H^0(C,Q_n) -> 0. Since the last space has dimension one and H^0(C,L_0)=k, dim_k H^0(C,L_n)=n+1 for every n>=0.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; vanishing and dimension calculation for every tensor power

proof.text: For each n>=0 the n+1 monomials s^{n-j}t^j, 0<=j<=n, form a basis of H^0(C,L_n). For n=0 this is the given k=H^0(C,O_C). Inductively, the image of t^{n+1} in Q_n is a local basis on D: in the local presentation of step 3 it has unit coefficient b^{n+1} modulo a. Because D is nonempty this section is nonzero, and spans the one-dimensional H^0(C,Q_n). Subtracting an appropriate k-multiple of t^{n+1} from any section of L_{n+1} therefore leaves s times a section of L_n. The induction gives spanning by the stated monomials, and the dimension n+2 from step 7 gives their linear independence. This is an explicit induction using the displayed exact sequences.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; multiplication and generation of the section ring

proof.text: Let B=direct_sum_{n>=0} H^0(C,L_n), with the section-ring multiplication. Sending the two degree-one variables S,T to s,t defines a graded k-algebra homomorphism k[S,T] -> B. On degree n it sends the polynomial basis S^{n-j}T^j to the basis of step 8; it is thus bijective in each degree, and therefore an isomorphism of graded rings. In degree zero it is exactly the canonical k -> H^0(C,O_C) from the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; the degree-one section ring is the polynomial ring

proof.text: The positive-degree ampleness criterion applies to this proper integral topological-dimension-one C and gives that M is ample, since deg_k M=1>0. Its structure map f:C -> Spec k is quasi-compact, as it is finite type. The only affine opens of Spec k are itself and the empty open, so M is also f-ample. The canonical-Proj criterion consequently supplies an open immersion r:C -> Proj_{Spec k}(direct_sum f_*L_n). Affine restriction of relative Proj identifies this target with Proj B; the graded isomorphism of step 9 identifies it over k with Proj k[S,T].

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; ampleness and the canonical map to Proj

proof.text: The coefficient map k tensor_Z Z[S,T] -> k[S,T], c tensor p |-> c p, is a graded k-algebra isomorphism: in each degree both sides have the same binary monomial basis, and these maps respect multiplication. The affine-Proj scalar-extension theorem for Z -> k now identifies Proj k[S,T] with Spec k times_{Spec Z} Proj Z[S,T], preserving structure maps. By the projective-space definition this is P({0,1};Spec k)=P^1_k. Thus r is a k-morphism and an open immersion into the precise projective line of the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; identification with the base-change definition of projective line

proof.text: Projective space over k is proper, hence separated. The proper-to-separated theorem applied to the proper C -> Spec k and the k-morphism r:C -> P^1_k makes r proper; a proper morphism is closed. Its image is consequently both open and closed, and is nonempty because C is integral. The two standard charts of P^1_k are Spec k[u] and Spec k[v]. Their intersection is obtained by inverting u and v, with v=u^{-1}, so the zero primes agree there. Each chart is irreducible: in the domain k[u] (respectively k[v]) the zero prime has the whole spectrum as closure. The common zero prime is therefore dense in both charts and in their union. Hence P^1_k is irreducible, so a nonempty open-and-closed subset is all of it. Thus r is a surjective open immersion, which by the definition of open immersion is an isomorphism of schemes over k, as required.

source.place: Tag 0C6T (lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree), degree-one specialization; the image in the projective line is the whole line

proof_origin.place: Tag 0C6T, lemma-genus-zero-positive-degree, specialized to degree one; binary-monomial induction spells out its multiplication argument, and generic ampleness/canonical-Proj results realize its final Proj step.
